levels.cognitiveLoadSummary: Teach sections average roughly 600 words of well-headed prose with recaps, and most are competently chunked, but the level is 100% passive: every visual is a plain-text table or arrow chain in a code fence and there is zero retrieval practice before the single design write. The heaviest offenders are reference-sheet lessons (template-pitfalls stacks six dense lists; latency-numbers is three raw memorization tables) and the four-topic core-entities-api lesson. The estimation module (m2) is the biggest interactivity win: one capacity-calc widget genuinely IS the concept for three of its four lessons. The method/communication lessons (m3/m4) are inherently prose-shaped and mostly need checks, not sims.

levels.cognitiveLoadSummary: This level is mechanism-heavy and its core mechanisms are temporal (handshakes, resolver walks, HOL blocking, retry races, breaker states), yet ten of the 21 lessons have zero diagrams of any kind and describe multi-step timelines entirely in prose; a single sequence widget with failure toggles would materially upgrade at least six lessons (DNS, TCP, TLS, idempotency, HTTP semantics, real-time comms). Three lessons map one-to-one onto existing vocabulary sims (cache-sim, queue-sim, lb-strategies). The densest lessons are cdn-caching-foundations (~720 words spanning five subtopics), request-lifecycle (an 11-step walk in one pass), and latency-percentiles (probability and queueing math with no manipulable visual). Named misconceptions are unusually frequent in the prose ('interview nuance' traps), making high-value checks easy to author.

levels.cognitiveLoadSummary: Every lesson is a single 600-950 word expert prose wall followed by one free-text design write; only 7 of 17 teaches have any visual at all, and each of those is a single ASCII fence. Load is dominated by named-mechanism enumerations (five read anomalies, three amplifications, eight database families, six ID/key subtopics) delivered back to back with no retrieval practice mid-teach. The lessons themselves repeatedly name likely misconceptions as 'interview nuance', which makes predict-then-reveal checks the cheapest high-leverage addition, while the storage-mechanics lessons (WAL commit path, isolation interleavings, LSM write path) are natural sequence/animated-diagram material.
